column7: Aiyari's old airstrip was cleared in the early 1990s. Cone markers were put in place for landing, but no landing ever took place. Around 1993, one flight circled above the airstrip but never made its first landing. Airstrip is not in operation.

The soccer field at Awaru was cleared in the early 2000s as an airstrip. It was cleared after flights to Sila stopped due to a clan dispute between two brothers over the airstrip there. Once the dispute was resolved and flights resumed at Sila, the Awaru airstrip was abandoned and later houses were built on part of the land and the remaining area became a soccer field.

Previously known as Christian Revival Center (CRC). Due to lack of financial support from the Mother Church, this small church pulled out from the mother church to seek support from the United Church. Currently supported by the United Church. The building currently serves two purposes. From Monday to Friday, Early Childhood Learning uses the building to teach school kids and on Sundays, building is used for worship.
The school operated until mid-2026 when a conflict arose between the two teachers, leading to a cessation of teaching activities. Consequently, student attendance ceased.

The current location of Dea Primary School was formerly the old Dea airstrip. It became unusable due to excessive mud and a short runway, and no other flights landed after it was initially cleared. The original Dea School was established at Taparuraha, located between Dea, Ugunomo, and Siribu villages. When the airstrip became non-operational, the school was relocated to the airstrip site as it needed an area accessible to the main road.
